correctness.rationale: For every implication-only term t, if its rightmost leaf is assigned 1 then t evaluates 1, yielding at least 1/4 agreeing assignments for any pair; x≈(x→y) attains exactly 1/4. An explicit truth-count induction constructs every j in [2^(m-1),2^m] using T=(A→x_(ell+1))∨ remaining variables, where ∨ is itself an implication-only term. Four agreement-equation families give, in order, [2^(n-2),2^(n-1)], [2^(n-1),5·2^(n-3)], [5·2^(n-3),3·2^(n-2)] and [3·2^(n-2),2^n]. Direct truth splits verify their formulas; n=2 and n=1 are explicit. No primitive constants are used. Thus the stated complete dyadic interval follows for arbitrary n. Independent bitmask evaluation confirmed 263 truth-count and 388 agreement witnesses through n=8 and exhaustive clone closure sizes (2,6,38,942) through n=4, including 888848 pair comparisons; finite evidence is not the universal proof.
